tickets.title: Third Avenue L stop closure pilot proposal
tickets.summary: A speaker who analyzed MTA trip data said closing the Third Avenue L stop would save riders significant time because only about 5% of riders board or leave there. He noted the stop is not a transfer station and is not wheelchair accessible. He asked the board to refer the idea to the transportation committee.

tickets.title: 11th Street bike storage and delivery worker conditions
tickets.summary: Over 100 electric delivery bikes are stored on 11th Street, obstructing the sidewalk and street, and nearby businesses and landlords report closures and vacancies. Delivery workers depend on the bikes and have no legal parking, and the precinct plans enforcement and bike confiscation starting October 7. Speakers asked for translated notice, outreach to worker groups, and a conversation about the history of the situation. Action: Coordinate with the precinct, sanitation, and elected officials on site options, translated notice, and the enforcement timeline before October 7.

tickets.title: Seward Park drug activity and park lighting
tickets.summary: Residents and park users report increased drug use and homelessness in Seward Park, and the Ecology Center reports drug users near its building's bathroom. Speakers also noted dark spots in the park that allow drug use to go unseen. The Parks Department and police have a task force, and the district manager said outreach providers are active. Action: Follow up with the Seventh Precinct, the Parks Department, and outreach providers on drug activity, and ask residents to report out-of-service lights to 311.

tickets.title: Mobile voting option for CEC elections
tickets.summary: A resolution asks the city to pilot a mobile-first voting option for Community Education Council elections because turnout is very low. Speakers said households without computers and parents not enrolled in the NYC schools account are excluded, and that outreach must clearly explain eligibility and data privacy for immigrant families. Action: Send the resolution urging the Department of Education to pilot mobile voting and expand multilingual parent outreach.

tickets.title: Essex Market RFP issuance and resolution concerns
tickets.summary: The RFP for Essex Market was expected to go out at the end of the month, but EDC did not clearly answer whether the board's resolutions were included. The joint land use and economic development committee wants the market kept community-run. Action: Ask EDC to postpone issuing the RFP and clarify how the board's resolutions are reflected, at a meeting this week.

tickets.title: Free public restroom pilot access and protocols
tickets.summary: The city is installing 17 free public restrooms as a one-year pilot, with two in the district, including one near Delancey Plaza. Access uses tap cards, QR codes, or an app, and the committee raised concerns about who can access the restrooms and emergency calls. DOT leads the pilot and a private contractor maintains the facilities. Action: Prepare a resolution next month setting out access and emergency protocols for the pilot.

tickets.title: Manhattan Bridge exits and Canal Street redesign update
tickets.summary: The board sent a letter to the mayor and DOT about safety concerns at the foot of the Manhattan Bridge, following a recent fatal crash. The letter also asked for an update on the Canal Street redesign, which has not been updated since January. Action: Follow up with the mayor and DOT for a response to the letter and an update on the Canal Street redesign.

tickets.title: FDR congestion impact from congestion pricing
tickets.summary: A member asked whether congestion pricing increased traffic on the FDR, as projected in the air quality report and an earlier board resolution. The member asked whether any reporting exists and whether the board could request it. Action: Ask MTA or DOT to report on actual FDR congestion impacts from congestion pricing and to return to the board.

tickets.title: MetroCard support for uptown immigrant center visitors
tickets.summary: A speaker asked whether transportation cost support such as OMNY or MetroCards will be offered to immigrants traveling to the new Manhattan Immigrant Welcome Center at 125th Street. The trip from the district often requires two to three transfers. Action: Raise the request for transportation cost support with the Manhattan Borough President's office.

tickets.title: NYCHA residents food, necessities, and communication access
tickets.summary: A caller said NYCHA residents in poverty lack food, water, and necessities and asked how they will get them. A hard-of-hearing caller said sign language and captioning communication access is essential for deaf residents. The caller also asked for help reducing drug activity and restoring ability to work. Action: Refer the NYCHA food, necessity, and communication access concerns to the appropriate city agencies for follow-up.

tickets.title: Proposed indoor roller skating facility on East River Pier
tickets.summary: A speaker proposed a 300,000 square foot multi-use indoor roller skating facility on the East River Pier, with admission set at $8. The proposal projects 250 to 500 jobs. Action: Refer the East River Pier roller skating proposal to the land use committee for review.

tickets.title: October vote on district needs and budget priorities
tickets.summary: The board will vote in October on its district needs statement and ranked expense and capital budget priorities for city agencies. The district manager noted the draft housing plan is 75% market rate, while affordable housing is the board's top need. Action: Hold the October vote on district needs and ranked agency budget priorities, emphasizing affordable housing.

tickets.title: Proposed bylaws changes on attendance and removal
tickets.summary: Proposed bylaw changes would give members a letter and an executive committee meeting after excess absences, rather than moving straight to removal. The changes also remove attendance from the removal process and require public members to follow conflict of interest policies. The bylaws require 28 days notice before the vote. Action: Circulate the proposed bylaws and hold the vote at the October full board meeting.

tickets.title: Board training on SLA, Robert's Rules, and office procedures
tickets.summary: The board chair announced planned trainings on SLA, Robert's Rules, and office procedures, with dates to be reported later. Members can email the chair with training topics or questions. Action: Set dates for the SLA, Robert's Rules, and office procedures trainings and report them to members.

tickets.title: Allen Street liquor license recommendation denial
tickets.summary: A member moved to deny an unlicensed Allen Street location tied to a former operator with problematic prior operations. The committee had earlier voted for conditions and noted the state could approve without stipulations if the board denies. The board voted 20 yes, 10 no, and 9 abstaining to deny. Action: Organize community members to attend the SLA hearing to support the denial and watch the SLA calendar.

tickets.title: August SLA resolution wording corrections for two locations
tickets.summary: Two August SLA resolutions contained wording errors that said full on-premises licenses where the applications were for beer and wine licenses, for Soft Hours Tea House and Cozy Cafe. The chair acknowledged the clerical errors. Action: Correct the resolution wording for Soft Hours Tea House and Cozy Cafe to read beer and wine license.
